newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bk of East Asia FRCD raised to HK$2.3bln.
newsitem.headline: Bk of East Asia FRCD raised to HK$2.3bln.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd's floating rate certificate of deposit issue due December 1999 has been increased to HK$2.3 billion from HK$1.8 billion due to oversubscription, arranger Societe Generale Asia said Tuesday.
The three-year certificates were priced at par and re-offered at a fixed 99.875. They pay a coupon of 37.5 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 44 basis points.
Application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the issue as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Twenty-three international banks in addition to the six arrangers joined the syndication.

Arrangers are China Development Finance Co (Hong Kong), with HK$170 million, and Bayerische Landesbank's Hong Kong branch, Societe Generale Asia, Sumitomo Finance (Asia), Union Bank of Switzerland's Hong Kong branch and Westpac Banking Corp's Hong Kong branch, with HK$125 million each.

Co-arrangers are DKB Asia with HK$120 million, Standard Chartered Bank with HK$110 million, Nippon Credit International (Hong Kong) with HK$105 million, Banca Commerciale Italiana's Hong Kong branch with HK$100 million, and Asahi Finance (Hong Kong), Banque Nationale de Paris's Hong Kong branch, Daiwa Securities (HK), Fuji International Finance (HK), JP Morgan Securities Asia, Merrill Lynch International and Sakura Finance Asia, with HK$90 million each.
Lead manager, ING Bank's Hong Kong branch, committed to HK$70 million.
Senior managers, with HK$50 million each, are CARIPLO's Hong Kong branch and DG Bank.

Managers, with HK$30 million each, are Banco Central Hispanoamericano's Hong Kong branch, Berliner Bank, BZW Asia, China Construction Bank's Hong Kong branch, Credit Lyonnais, LTCB Asia, Sanwa International Finance, Schroders Asia and Thai Farmers Bank's Hong Kong branch.
